title: Remote-Piloted Robot Workcells for Returns Processing
one_liner: Two-arm teleoperated stations in US returns centers, piloted by trained remote workers in low-wage regions, priced per item and generating the data to automate each task over time.
customer: Reverse-logistics processors, e-commerce returns centers, refurbishers and 3PLs handling apparel and consumer electronics in high-wage regions.
problem: Returns are high-variance and every item is different, so they are labor-heavy, high-turnover and hard to automate. Pure autonomy is not ready and pure teleop is too slow: early stations may run at only 30-50% of human speed, so hourly pricing fails.
solution: Deploy open-source dual-arm stations (ALOHA-class, about $30k each) where remote pilots handle exceptions and supervise learned behaviors on routine items. Price per item processed, guaranteed 20-30% below local labor, and let one pilot cover 3-5 stations as autonomy improves. Every pilot hour becomes licensable training data.
why_now: Cheap arms, open-source teleop rigs and robot-learning models are good enough for supervised autonomy. XDOF's $50M annualized revenue shows the teleop-data market pays, and 1X's teleoperated NEO shows buyers already accept a human in the loop.
revenue_model: $0.40-1.20 per item processed, with data licensing to model developers as an additional revenue stream.
non_obvious_insight: The teleop-versus-autonomy debate is a false dichotomy for buyers who pay per outcome. The economic robot today is a pilot-supervised robot whose human share falls every month, so the transitional business earns money while producing the data rivals pay for. It only works if you price per item and measure interventions per hour honestly.
first_30_days: Partner with one returns processor. Deploy 2 open-source stations on 2 tasks (test and grade electronics accessories, re-bag apparel), recruit 6 pilots through a Philippine BPO partner, and sell a 90-day pilot at a per-item price.

title: Live Herd Maps for Hiking Apps
one_liner: Collar-derived herd positions pushed to hiking and mountain-bike apps so hikers reroute around cattle, funded by the destination that profits from the landscape.
customer: Alpine and mountain destination bodies, municipalities and trail associations paying for a valley licence. Secondary buyers are livestock-liability insurers and the trail apps themselves as distribution partners.
problem: Cattle-hiker incidents have produced large liability judgments in the Alps (reported in Tyrol and elsewhere), pushing farmers to fence trails or abandon high pastures, which erodes the landscape tourists come for. Hiker density is rising with overtourism. The farmer knows where the cows are, and virtual-fencing and GPS collars already record it, but the hiker does not.
solution: Ingest positions from virtual-fencing and GPS collars and cheap satellite or LoRa tags, and publish geofenced herd zones at roughly 30-minute freshness through an open API to trail apps such as Outdooractive, Komoot, AllTrails and Gaia. Add trailhead QR and SMS warnings and detour suggestions. The incident log becomes the farmer's dated proof of warnings issued, which supports liability cover and premium credits. A US variant covers guardian-dog and cattle conflicts on western grazing allotments.
why_now: Virtual-fencing collars (Halter, Nofence) have scaled from pilots to fleets, and satellite IoT now covers valleys without cell service. International arrivals hit about 1.52B in 2025, and Spain, Italy and Japan are all trying to move visitors off crowded routes. Destinations have new levies and budgets to spend on dispersal.
revenue_model: EUR12K-EUR40K/yr per valley from destination bodies. A collar-vendor or farmer data fee of EUR3-EUR6 per collar per month. Insurer data licences and app API fees.
non_obvious_insight: The herd data is a by-product already collected for a different reason, and the liability problem is fundamentally an information problem. Selling to the destination rather than the farmer solves who pays, because the destination's product is the pastoral landscape.
first_30_days: Pick one valley (Tyrol, Graubunden or Colorado) with an existing collar deployment, and sign the destination body and farmers' cooperative to a summer-2027 pilot by March. Build a GPX geofence feed and get one trail app to test it as a data partner.

title: The Master's Letter Apprenticeships
one_liner: Six-week, premium apprenticeships with master craftspeople that give teens the one credential AI cannot counterfeit: a named human's signed, callable letter about what they actually did.
customer: Affluent parents of 15-18 year olds (private-school and college-admissions-anxious) paying $6-12k per placement. Masters (luthiers, boat-builders, stone masons, pastry chefs, bookbinders, restoration carpenters, farriers) get 60% of tuition.
problem: Application essays are AI-contaminated, and admissions offices are shifting to in-person writing, short answers, and interviews because they can't trust take-home work. Wealthy families are hunting for hard-to-fake, embodied, verifiable experiences. Meanwhile master craftspeople in aging trades lack apprentices and income to take them on.
solution: A curated roster of about 40 masters per metro. Structured 6-week apprenticeships on real work, not shadowing. Each ends in a finished object with the maker's mark and a Master's Letter written to a rubric, backed by a recorded interview and a verification page colleges can call. An alumni network and independent counselors' referral fees drive supply of students.
why_now: Admissions officers openly discount take-home writing and are moving to formats that are harder to fake. Entry-level white-collar hiring is shrinking (Stanford payroll data show early-career workers in AI-exposed jobs losing ground), which raises the prestige and perceived safety of craft. Aging masters have shops and no successors.
revenue_model: 25-40% platform fee on $6-12k tuition. Corporate- or foundation-sponsored scholarship seats. $900 'Family Master Day' add-ons.
non_obvious_insight: The product isn't the skill. It is a third-party attested effort signed by a reputationally exposed human. A letter from a master who stakes their name is the analog of the old handwritten recommendation, now scarce. The supply side is an underused asset: elderly masters with empty workbenches.
first_30_days: Recruit 8 masters in one city through trade guilds. Publish a landing page. Recruit 5-10 independent college counselors as referral partners at 10%. Sell 12 slots for summer 2027 starting in the winter admissions-anxiety season. Get background checks and liability insurance in place.

title: Crawlspace Robots for the 44-Year-Old House
one_liner: Small tracked robots that scan, photograph and eventually air-seal and insulate the crawlspaces and attics humans dread, starting as a quote-enabling survey service.
customer: Home inspectors, insurers and home-warranty firms (moisture and water-damage claims), and HVAC, insulation and foundation-repair contractors who need access before quoting. Later: weatherization programs.
problem: Median home age is 44 years, 62% of homeowners now choose repair over replace, and 78% of those with unstarted projects have no quotes. Contractors avoid the crawlspace visit because it is slow, dirty and unsafe, so inspectors skip it and quotes are guesses. It is the most avoided labor in the house.
solution: Phase 1: a low-cost tracked robot with camera, thermal and LiDAR plus a vision-language pipeline producing a 10-minute survey covering moisture, insulation, duct leaks, pest and mold signs and structural issues, sold as an add-on to inspectors and a pre-quote survey to contractors. Phase 2: tool attachments for air sealing and topping insulation. Phase 3: crawlspace-as-a-service retrofit fleet.
why_now: Cheap edge compute, reliable vision-language defect classification and low-cost thermal sensors. Labor shortages make anyone willing to crawl scarce. Insurers want moisture data and aging stock keeps growing.
revenue_model: $149-249 per survey (inspector add-on or contractor pre-quote), insurer report fees, later per-job retrofit revenue.
non_obvious_insight: The robot does not need to replace skilled trades, only the worst 20 minutes of their job. Access is the friction, and a proprietary library of real crawlspace conditions is the moat.
first_30_days: Build v0 from a hobby tracked chassis, action camera and thermal sensor (about $3K). Run 30 free surveys for 5 home inspectors and 2 insulation contractors. Track how often findings convert to jobs and test pricing.

title: Royalty-Exact Generators: One Adapter per Creator
one_liner: A generative sound-effects and sample tool where every contributor has their own adapter, so payouts are exact by construction instead of guessed after the fact.
customer: Indie game developers, video editors and YouTubers buying sound effects and samples (paying users), with foley artists and sample-pack producers as the opt-in supply side.
problem: Attribution in generative AI is post-hoc guesswork: the Spotify-UMG covers deal promises credit and compensation but discloses no tracking method. Small creators are excluded from label-scale licensing deals. Buyers want output they can use commercially without a legal cloud.
solution: Fine-tune a small open text-to-audio model with a separate adapter per consenting creator. Each generation composes adapters with explicit weights, and royalties follow those weights, so attribution is bookkeeping rather than research. Every output carries a watermark and a per-generation receipt. Start with short sound effects and foley, where inference is cheap, demand is high and buyers' licensing needs are simple.
why_now: Adapter fine-tuning is cheap, Suno's Sep 9 switch to licensed training shows licensed models are becoming the norm, and the credit-and-compensation gap in the Spotify-UMG deal is visible.
revenue_model: $15-50/month subscriptions plus usage credits, with 60-70% distributed to adapter owners pro rata, and enterprise indemnified licenses for studios.
non_obvious_insight: Attribution research tries to recover influence from a monolithic model. Changing the architecture turns attribution into accounting, and small, narrow, licensed models beat large generic ones on legal risk.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 foley artists and sample makers via forums and Gumroad and itch.io sellers. Fine-tune adapters on an open SFX model, demo composite generations with receipts, and pre-sell $99 annual plans to 100 indie developers via itch.io and Discord.

title: Help-Desk Reset Firewall for MSPs
one_liner: A plug-in for ConnectWise, Autotask and HaloPSA that makes it impossible for a technician to reset a password or MFA without out-of-band verification and manager approval.
customer: MSPs and outsourced IT help desks serving SMBs, priced per technician.
problem: IT help desks are a named target of voice deepfakes, and one report says over half of CISOs have seen a successful attack. An MSP technician is a single point of compromise for dozens of client tenants, and techs judge identity by voice and by facts attackers already have. SMB clients have no security team to catch it.
solution: A reset gate inside the ticket. MFA resets, password resets and new-device enrollments require verification through a contact and number pulled from the client's HR system or PSA (never from the caller), a manager approval push, a cooling-off delay with notification to the user's existing devices, and risk scoring (new country, odd hours). Evidence is stored for insurer questionnaires.
why_now: Help-desk social engineering drove major 2025 intrusions, voice cloning removes the tell, and insurers now ask about caller verification. Enterprise help-desk verification vendors ignore the MSP channel.
revenue_model: $15-30 per technician per month plus $1 per client user per month.
non_obvious_insight: MSPs are the most leveraged and least-served target. The control is a process lock, not a detector, so it does not decay when deepfakes improve, and insurance-renewal pressure makes it a required purchase.
first_30_days: Build it as a ConnectWise Manage/HaloPSA webhook plus a Teams approval bot. Recruit 10 MSPs from MSP peer groups and forums at $299 per month, and show the insurance-renewal benefit.

title: Escrowed Group Orders for Fandom Imports
one_liner: A group-order platform for K-pop, anime and idol merchandise that escrows money, consolidates freight under formal customs entry, and splits domestic shipping.
customer: Group-order managers (volunteer fans running orders on X, Instagram and Discord) and the fans who join their orders, plus small importers.
problem: US de minimis ended on 29 Aug 2025, so single parcels from Korea can be dutiable. Group orders run on PayPal Friends and Family and trust, and fraud is rife: Korea's police reported foreign-national fraud complaints rising from 5,307 (2023) to 19,907 (2025). Group-order managers personally carry the customs and refund risk.
solution: Managers list an order, participants pay into escrow, we purchase against verified receipts and aggregate into one commercial shipment (broker-filed entry, duties and product-safety rules handled), then split to US addresses with tracking. A reputation score for managers and automatic refunds when an order fails.
why_now: The de minimis change turned informal parcel-splitting into an importer-of-record problem, and scam volume is surging.
revenue_model: A 4-6% escrow fee, a freight and handling margin, and a manager subscription for tools.
non_obvious_insight: The informal fan trust economy has no importer and no escrow. Whoever becomes the compliant importer of record plus payment escrow captures the volume, because managers cannot solve duty on their own.
first_30_days: Partner with 5 mid-size US group-order managers. Run 3 orders end to end through a Korean freight forwarder. Charge the escrow fee and publish a public scam tracker for credibility.

title: Second-Look Verification for Imagery-Based Nonrenewals
one_liner: A $50-80, 48-hour human check between an aerial-imagery flag and a nonrenewal, sold to carriers' compliance teams.
customer: Regional and mid-size homeowners carriers and MGAs in California, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania and New York, bought by underwriting and compliance leads.
problem: Imagery-driven nonrenewals are generating regulatory heat (a Florida owner with 52 claim-free years was dropped with no inspection). California AB 75 became operative July 1 2026, requiring notice, a copy of the photos, a dispute path and a remediation window. CT, NH and PA regulators say imagery alone is insufficient, and a NY bill is pending. In-person inspections cost far more and take weeks.
solution: A guided homeowner video capture with fraud checks, or a local gig inspector, returning structured findings mapped to the carrier's rules. It auto-generates the compliant notice package and remediation checklist, and keeps an audit log for regulators.
why_now: AB 75 took effect July 1 2026, and other states are moving.
revenue_model: Per flagged policy plus a platform fee.
non_obvious_insight: Regulators demand more than imagery, but nobody wants $250 inspections. The lower price point makes compliance affordable at scale and sells to a budget-holding compliance team.
first_30_days: Call 10 regional carriers' compliance heads and pilot with 200 flagged policies. Prove the share of imagery flags that human review clears.

title: Landowner-Side Broker for Data-Center Land
one_liner: A conflict-free advocate that scores your parcel's power value and runs a competitive process, so the family farm isn't sold cheap to an anonymous LLC.
customer: Family landowners with 100-2,000 acres near high-voltage transmission lines or substations, in data-center-active counties, who are getting unsolicited offers. Each deal is worth $5-50M or more.
problem: Developers approach landowners through shell LLCs and landmen, with NDAs and options that lock the land up cheaply. Landowners can't tell whether $30K or $300K an acre is fair, because value now depends on grid interconnection position, water and fiber rather than acreage. Regional brokers don't know how to value power, so owners either sell too low or refuse offers that are actually good.
solution: A licensed landowner-side brokerage. A Parcel Power Score built from public transmission and substation data, utility large-load tariffs, zoning and moratorium status, water and fiber proximity, and an independent power engineer's review. It runs a competitive process to many site-selection teams and developers, negotiates terms (sale, option, lease, JV, decommissioning bonds), and represents only the seller.
why_now: Land purchases for future data centers reached about $6B in the first half of 2026, up roughly 79% from a year earlier (Avison Young), and sale offers in some places run up to 10 times agricultural value. Sept 2026 coverage shows farmers getting huge offers alongside a local backlash and moratoria that make timing and zoning risk decisive. The seller-side infrastructure has not caught up.
revenue_model: $5-15K representation retainer that is credited against a 1-2% success fee. On $10-50M deals this is $100-500K per closing. Optional fee for a second-opinion review of an existing offer.
non_obvious_insight: Land in this market is priced on power queue position, not soil. Buyers know it and sellers don't, and that information gap is the fee pool. Being seller-only and publishing the methodology makes you the trusted party for landowners and gives hyperscalers a pre-assembled, pre-screened pipeline they will actually prefer. The parcel data is a compounding asset.
first_30_days: Pick a cluster of counties around a substation or 345kV corridor in a data-center-active area (for example Ohio, Indiana, Georgia, Texas or Pennsylvania). Build parcel maps with public HIFLD and county data. Mail or door-knock 300 landowners with a free Parcel Power Score. Partner with a rural land attorney and an independent power engineer, get a broker license or partner with a licensed broker, and aim to sign 3 exclusive representation agreements. Send a one-page buyer package to 20 site-selection teams.

title: Notary Network for Human-Verified Hiring
one_liner: Bonded local human witnesses (mostly mobile notaries and loan-signing agents) sit with a job candidate for a phone-free live work sample and sign an attestation the employer can rely on.
customer: Remote-first companies of 20-2,000 people hiring for roles that touch code, money, patient data or production systems (fintech, health-tech, cybersecurity, engineering, back-office BPO), plus staffing and recruiting agencies placing remote workers. The first buyer is a 30-person startup that cannot fly candidates to HQ.
problem: Video interviews are no longer trustworthy evidence of who is doing the work. Real-time face-swaps, proxy test-takers and AI feeding answers are common: a 2026 Greenhouse survey reportedly found 91% of US hiring managers had encountered or suspected AI-generated answers, and Gartner projects that by 2028 one in four candidate profiles will be synthetic. Google and McKinsey reportedly reintroduced in-person verification steps, but a small remote employer cannot fly every finalist in, and detection software is an arms race the defenders keep losing.
solution: A marketplace of vetted, insured, background-checked local witnesses. The candidate meets one at a library room or coworking space. The witness checks government ID in person, hands the candidate a locked-down laptop or a paper packet, and stays through a 60-90 minute live work sample or technical interview run by the employer over the employer's own video call. No phones are allowed in the room. The witness signs a notarial-style attestation (ID match, unbroken presence, session log, photo) that goes into the employer's applicant file. Sold as a $150-250 per-session add-on to the final-round interview. The same primitive later extends to bootcamp and university oral exams, licensing bodies, and witnessed authorship for authors and artists.
why_now: In 2026, deepfake candidates are ranked among the top fraud threats by Experian, and hiring teams are openly adding in-person checks. Meanwhile mortgage volume is still well below its 2021 peak, so tens of thousands of trained loan-signing agents have idle capacity and already know how to verify identity and witness a signature. Remote notarization and gig onboarding tools make a distributed 1099 witness network cheap to stand up.
revenue_model: Employers pay $150-250 per attested session (witness keeps roughly 55%). Subscription tiers for volume hirers ($500-2,000 per month with session credits). Enterprise and staffing-agency contracts with bulk pricing. Later: per-exam fees from education and credentialing bodies.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not better deepfake detection but a cheap, trusted, physical human at a known place, and the law already has an institution for that: the notary. A loan-signing workforce is already trained, insured and idle. The purchase also gets filed under fraud and insider-risk compliance (nation-state fake-IT-worker schemes, SOC 2 evidence) rather than HR, which means bigger budgets and faster approval.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 signing agents in three metros through notary Facebook groups and NotaryCafe-type forums, with a simple 1099 onboarding. Write the session protocol and attestation PDF in a week; run booking and payment with Airtable and Stripe. Cold-email 100 remote-heavy startups and staffing firms with the offer 'we will send a human to sit with your finalist, first 3 sessions at $99'. Aim for 10 paid sessions by day 30. Publish an anonymized case study of the first mismatch or coached-answer catch.

title: Provably Anonymous, Provably Employee Whistleblower Channel
one_liner: A reporting channel where a worker proves they hold a company email using zero-knowledge proofs, without the employer or vendor ever learning who they are.
customer: EU and UK employers with 50-500 staff that must run internal reporting channels, employment-law and compliance firms that deploy them, and works councils.
problem: Whistleblower-directive compliance is often a checkbox. Employees do not believe 'anonymous' hotlines that log IPs and identities, so use is low. Employers get junk or spoofed reports and cannot confirm that a reporter is a real current employee.
solution: ZK-email proofs of an employer-domain, DKIM-signed message let a reporter prove employment without revealing which mailbox. Per-report nullifiers block duplicates, and no identity is stored. Add anonymous two-way messaging, evidence upload, and a 'verified current employee in a group of at least 10' signal to the company. Independent cryptographic review is published.
why_now: ZK-email tooling is open source and maturing, EU digital-identity wallets are due by end 2026, and deepfake and spoofed reports are increasing. Whistleblower rules now apply to smaller firms, so many companies are buying cheap channels for the first time.
revenue_model: EUR 300-1,500 per month per company, with a 30% channel margin for law firms and a free tier for firms under 50 staff.
non_obvious_insight: Hotline usage is limited by trust in anonymity, which promises cannot improve, only making identification cryptographically impossible can. The same proof gives employers what they want (verified employee) and gives hostile insiders nothing.
first_30_days: Prototype with open-source zk-email libraries. Line up three employment-law firms and 10 SMEs for a free pilot, and commission a small third-party cryptography review to publish.

title: Closing Ceremonies for Layoffs and Team Sunsets
one_liner: Trained ex-chaplains and celebrants who design and run dignified endings for teams hit by AI-driven layoffs, project sunsets and site closures.
customer: HR and people leaders at mid-size and large firms (500-5,000 employees) restructuring around AI, and outplacement firms that want to bundle a meaning-making service.
problem: Challenger reports AI was cited in about 112,713 announced US job cuts through July 2026 (about 24% of all cuts) and has led all reasons for five straight months. Layoffs are still delivered in a 15-minute video call and followed by résumé workshops. Nobody marks what ended, so leavers feel discarded, survivors feel guilty and disengage, and the company inherits hostile alumni.
solution: A 'Closing' package after legal communications are done: a facilitated last-day ceremony with a witness circle, a symbolic hand-off of work, a leaver-alumni charter (references, introductions), a manager script that bans corporate euphemism, and a survivor circle a week later. It is delivered in person or on video by a trained celebrant or ex-chaplain.
why_now: AI-attributed layoffs have become the leading cause of job cuts in 2026, and waves are recurring. Employer brand and alumni networks now matter for boomerang hiring and recruiting, and workers are openly sceptical of 'AI restructuring' messaging.
revenue_model: $4-12k per event, annual retainers of roughly $30-100k for an 'endings desk' that supports repeated restructurings, per-seat training licences for managers, and channel fees from outplacement partners.
non_obvious_insight: Companies overspend on what people do next and underspend on acknowledging what just ended. A layoff is a funeral without a ritual, and the missing ritual is the root of downstream problems: regretted attrition, employer-brand damage and lost referrals. A ceremony costs a tiny fraction of severance and is the only lever that changes how people talk about the company afterwards.
first_30_days: Recruit three ex-chaplains or celebrants. Build a 2-hour and a half-day format with a legal-review partner. Approach 15 outplacement consultants and 30 people-operations leaders, and offer one discounted team pilot in exchange for a case study.

title: Glasses-Free Zone: Smart-Glasses Detection Kits
one_liner: A detection-plus-policy kit for rooms where camera glasses cannot be allowed (exam centers, courtrooms, medical rooms, locker rooms, poker rooms), with logged, defensible procedures.
customer: Independent test centers, licensing and language-test operators, court administrators, casinos and poker rooms, med-spas, therapy and medical offices, gyms and locker-room operators.
problem: Camera and AI glasses look like ordinary eyewear and are now cheap and everywhere. Venues have bans on paper but no way to enforce or prove violations. In May 2026 two TOEIC test-takers were caught with AI glasses and banned for four years. The College Board banned smart glasses (even prescription ones) at the SAT starting March 2026, and New York State courts banned them across all courthouses in 2026.
solution: A door-frame or desk unit combining Bluetooth and Wi-Fi signature scanning for known glasses families, plus an optional optical check for camera lenses. It ships with a written policy pack, non-accusatory staff scripts, signage, a tamper-evident event log usable in score-invalidation or eviction disputes, and a short staff certification. The software updates as new glasses launch.
why_now: Camera-and-AI glasses went mainstream in 2025 to 2026, and other brands are launching. Institutions responded with bans in months, but incumbents (exam vendors, courts, gyms) have no tooling or procedures. The 18-month gap is between glasses in millions of faces and venue-grade controls. Consumer detector apps exist, but no one owns the evidence-grade, staff-friendly layer.
revenue_model: $299 to $999 policy and training kit, $1,500 to $5,000 per site for hardware install, then $49 to $149 per month for signature updates, incident logging and re-certification.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer's problem isn't detection accuracy, it's defensibility. A test center that cancels a score or a court that ejects a spectator needs a repeatable, logged, non-accusatory process to survive an appeal or a complaint. Sell the paper trail and the staff script, and treat the sensor as an accessory. False accusations, not misses, are what scare institutions.
first_30_days: Build a prototype scanner on an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi with known Bluetooth signatures from Ray-Ban Meta and other glasses, and test on real devices. Write the policy kit with an ex-proctor or court-security advisor. Offer paid pilots to 10 independent test-prep and test centers, one poker room and two med-spas. Charge for the kit from the start.

title: Medicaid Hours Wallet for Gig Workers
one_liner: A phone-based monthly proof-of-work ledger that turns gig, cash and self-employment activity into state-accepted documentation and 30-day cure packets, paid for by the Medicaid plans and health centers that lose revenue when members drop.
customer: Medicaid managed care organizations with expansion-adult lines, and FQHC and community health center networks. Medicaid is 43-50% of health center revenue, and an MCO is paid capitation per member-month. End users are expansion adults aged 19-64 with irregular income. The MCO or health center pays per retained member; the enrollee pays nothing.
problem: CMS's interim final rule (June 3, 2026) requires states to implement 80 hours a month of work or activity, or $580 a month in income, by Jan 1, 2027. Compliance is checked at application and at renewal, and a noncompliance notice gives 30 calendar days to cure. CBO projects about 4.8M coverage losses from work requirements, largely from reporting complexity. About 9 in 10 affected patients are expected to qualify for an exemption or already comply, yet many will still lose coverage on documentation. Nebraska went live May 1, 2026 with self-attestation, but about 28,000 people there must document twice a year and the state plans to move to verification.
solution: An enrollee-side SMS and app tool. It ingests bank and payment-app statements, gig platform earnings exports (Uber, DoorDash, Cash App, Venmo), pay stub photos and logged volunteer or class hours. It computes whether each month clears $580 or 80 hours and generates the state-specific verification packet. It sends look-back-month reminders and prepares the 30-day cure response. It flags likely exemption candidates, such as medically frail members, from plan claims data. The plan or clinic dashboard shows at-risk members and cure success. The tool only assists and never determines compliance, which is what federal rules allow plans to do.
why_now: The interim final rule was published June 3, 2026, and the national start date is Jan 1, 2027. Nebraska's live rollout is the preview of what other states will face when verification replaces self-attestation. CMS is encouraging automation, but states are spending on caseworker portals, notices and screening tools, not on income documentation for gig workers.
revenue_model: $3-8 per at-risk member per month billed to the MCO, or a success fee of $50-150 per member retained through renewal. FQHC SaaS at $2-5k per month per site with an outcomes dashboard. Later, state contracts for a self-employed and gig documentation module.
non_obvious_insight: Vendors such as Salesforce are building state-facing portals for applicants and caseworkers. The parties with a P&L at stake, the MCOs and health centers, are not yet being sold a member-side tool. KFF's roundup of state outreach plans covers notices, websites and screening tools but does not describe how self-employed or irregular income will be documented (https://www.kff.org/medicaid/medicaid-work-requirements-federal-outreach-requirements-and-state-plans/). State wage-data matching misses 1099, cash and gig work by design. Georgetown's CCF warns that 'verification in this context means burdensome documentation requirements for enrollees' (https://ccf.georgetown.edu/2026/05/11/the-new-medicaid-work-reporting-requirements-are-here-dont-let-the-nebraska-soft-start-fool-you/). The retention math is lopsided: a plan or clinic can pay a few dollars a month per member to protect several hundred dollars of monthly revenue. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/03/2026-11094/medicaid-program-community-engagement-requirement-for-certain-individuals and https://www.pointcare.com/blog/how-to-prevent-medicaid-coverage-gaps-in-2026
first_30_days: Build the Nebraska flow first, since it is already live. Recruit 50 gig and self-employed Medicaid enrollees through one FQHC partner. Measure how many can produce a compliant $580 or 80-hour packet within 30 days. Take those results to two MCO member-engagement and quality leads for a paid pilot. Sign an LOI with one health center network before Jan 1, 2027.

title: Aftermarket Support for Stranded DJI Fleets
one_liner: Repair, rebuilt batteries, parts and firmware-independence retrofits for the many legally owned DJI drones that can no longer be replaced with new models.
customer: Police and fire drone units, agricultural spray operators, land surveyors, roofing and solar inspectors, and small public-safety departments with grant money.
problem: The FCC barred new DJI and Autel models in December 2025, US drone tariffs took effect in September 2026 (component tariffs follow in 2027), and China's export controls now cover motors, batteries, radios and sensors. Existing fleets stay legal to fly but face scarce parts and no assured US repair path.
solution: A US repair depot with stocked parts, rebuilt batteries using allied-source cells, gimbal and camera swaps, and open flight-controller retrofits (ArduPilot/PX4) as a migration path. Offer a per-drone maintenance plan with predictive service, and trade-in credits toward US-made airframes, which also become a lead source for those makers.
why_now: The December 2025 FCC action, September 2026 tariffs and export controls all landed within a year. The installed base is large and aging, and no one has a business focused on serving it.
revenue_model: $150-800 per repair, $30-80 per drone per month for maintenance plans, battery and parts sales, and referral fees from US airframe makers on trade-ins.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone debates who replaces DJI, while nobody serves the installed base for the next 5 years. Service earns higher margin than building a competing airframe, starts faster, and gives you the customer list every US-made airframe maker wants.
first_30_days: Buy 20 broken Mavic and Matrice units on secondary markets and set up a bench. Pitch fixed-price maintenance plans to 30 sheriff drone units and agricultural spraying co-ops, and sell the first 10 plans.

title: Refundable-Deposit Demand Proof for Indie Hardware
one_liner: A hosted reservation page that lets small hardware creators collect refundable $20-$50 deposits at tiered locked prices, giving them price-elasticity data and a demand certificate before they commit to a campaign or a factory MOQ.
customer: First- and second-time hardware and game creators planning a Kickstarter or Indiegogo launch, plus the small factories and pledge-manager agencies that advise them. Payer is the creator.
problem: Kickstarter median funding is $7,060 versus a $64,567 average, and Indiegogo's top performers all 'arrived with an audience already built.' Small creators have followers but no proof anyone will pay, so they either launch blind or over-order inventory.
solution: A Stripe Connect-based landing page where each deposit charges the creator's own account (no funds held by us) and is refunded on request. Visitors choose among three locked-in price tiers (A/B-testing price), and a referral queue rewards sharing. The dashboard shows deposit count by country, price-tier elasticity and expected launch-day conversion. A 'demand certificate' PDF can be handed to factories negotiating MOQ or to lenders offering inventory financing. Deposits convert with one click to day-one pledges on launch.
why_now: Big brands proved the pattern in 2025-26. eufyMake ran a $50 deposit to lock a $1,499 price before its April 2025 Kickstarter and raised over $10M in 14 hours. Creality's refundable $50 deposit unlocked a $649 VIP price for its filament maker, and the goal was hit in about 16.5 minutes. Meanwhile Indiegogo retired Flexible Funding in October 2025, so both platforms are all-or-nothing and the cost of launching without proof is higher.
revenue_model: $299 setup plus 1.5% of deposits processed, a $999 launch-readiness package (demand certificate, pricing test, launch-day email sequence), and $49/mo for post-launch late-pledge and pre-order pages.
non_obvious_insight: The most successful launches of 2025-26 did not start on Kickstarter. They started with money-backed waitlists. eufyMake opened a $50 deposit pre-order scheme to lock a $1,499 price ahead of the April 29 Kickstarter (https://www.notebookcheck.net/Anker-EufyMake-E1-UV-printer-Pre-order-deposit-scheme-now-open.999622.0.html) and then raised $46.76M from 17,822 backers (https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/3d-printer-breaks-kickstarter-record-raises-44m/493857). Creality took $50 refundable deposits for VIP $649 pricing on the M1 (https://makers101.com/creality-filament-maker-m1-shredder-r1-live-tracker/). Kickstarter's own pre-launch page only collects follows, and the ecosystem is top-heavy (median $7,060 vs average $64,567, and 'all Indiegogo top performers arrived with an audience', https://www.tcf.team/blog/q1-2026-crowdfunding-report). A deposit is a far stronger demand signal than a follower, and small creators have no tool to run one, no way to test three price points, and no artefact factories will trust.
first_30_days: Build the landing page and Stripe Connect flow in 2 weeks. Pitch 10 creators with live 'coming soon' pages on Kickstarter, offering a free pilot in exchange for a case study. Run a $20-$50 deposit test with one creator (target 150+ deposits) and document the elasticity result. Publish the case study on r/Kickstarter, BackerKit-focused groups and crowdfunding Discords, then charge the next 5 creators.

title: Import Compliance Desk for Hobby Brands
one_liner: Subscription compliance for small tabletop, designer-toy, card-accessory and collectible brands covering CPSC eFiling, product certificates, EU representative and tariff classification.
customer: Indie designer-toy studios, board-game and miniature publishers, Kickstarter creators and card-accessory brands importing from Asia or selling into the EU and UK, with $0.5M-$20M in revenue.
problem: CPSC electronic certificate filing for regulated imports became mandatory on 8 July 2026 (no value-based exemption; foreign-trade-zone entries follow 8 Jan 2027). The EU requires a responsible person for consumer products. De minimis ended in Aug 2025, so small parcels are dutiable. Hobby brands have no compliance staff, and blind-box and collectible toys straddle the children's-product line.
solution: Per-SKU compliance dossiers (accredited lab test-report management, certificate generation, filing data handed to brokers), classification lookups, an EU authorized-representative service, label review, and a landed-cost API for the brand's storefront.
why_now: eFiling is live, counterfeit-toy seizures show heightened customs attention, and crowdfunded creators are hitting duty surprises for the first time.
revenue_model: $199-999/month plus $150-500 per-SKU dossier fees and an EU representative fee.
non_obvious_insight: Hobby brands do not hire compliance, and backers forgive late delivery but not a customs seizure. Vertical-specific rulings (dice, sleeves, miniatures, plush) are reusable across every customer, which is what makes a generic compliance vendor less useful.
first_30_days: Sell a $299 eFiling readiness audit to 15 publishers via BoardGameGeek and Kickstarter creator communities. Partner with one customs broker and one accredited lab.

title: Waze for Agents: Live Bureaucracy Route Data
one_liner: A pay-per-lookup feed of the current, tested state of consumer and government web procedures (form changes, outages, hidden requirements, real step timings), sold to browser agents just before they attempt an errand.
customer: Browser and computer-use agents, and the agent platforms that run them, paying $0.005-$0.10 per route lookup via x402 or MPP. The heaviest users will be agents doing errands: license renewals, permits, benefits applications, insurance claims, utility transfers, refunds.
problem: Procedure websites change weekly with no changelog. Every failed attempt burns tokens, and worse, can leave a half-finished irreversible state such as a submitted but unpaid renewal. Every agent relearns the same breakages, and nobody pools that knowledge.
solution: Two data engines. First, synthetic canaries: daily automated dry-runs of the top ~500 US flows (state DMV and DOL, county property tax, SSA/IRS/USCIS account setup, top utilities, top insurers' claim portals, airline refund forms). They record schema diffs, required documents, CAPTCHAs, session timeouts and upload limits, and publish step-by-step 'route cards' with a success rate and freshness timestamp. Second, opt-in failure telemetry from customer agents, traded for credits, which covers the long tail Waze-style. Customers get a 'route guarantee': if a route verified in the last 24 hours fails, the lookup is refunded.
why_now: Browser agents moved from demo to production in 2026, with vendors reporting thousands of automated workflows per week on legacy portals. x402 and MPP make $0.01 lookups collectable without accounts. Governments are still not publishing agent-readable metadata.
revenue_model: Metered lookups, plus $500-$5,000/month platform plans for agent vendors that include telemetry credits. Premium verified-fresh routes for high-stakes flows, and later aggregate breakage analytics sold to agencies who want to fix their own forms.
non_obvious_insight: For an agent the scarce input is not information but freshness plus negative results: knowing what broke this morning. Agents' own failures are the raw material, so each new customer improves the map, a data network effect a static scraper cannot copy. Government sites are the one part of the web nobody will ever optimize for agents, which keeps the drift problem permanent.
first_30_days: Write 50 Playwright canaries for the 10 highest-traffic flows in 5 large states, using a cheap model to diff DOM and field schemas. Publish a free MCP server and a public 'status page for bureaucracy' to draw agent builders. Offer free credits to 5 browser-agent startups in exchange for telemetry, and start charging in month 3 once the route guarantee has a track record.

title: Vet-Verified Escrow for Puppy Purchases
angle: Finance (payments, scams) x Pets & animal health (vet access, insurance)
one_liner: Buyer funds sit in escrow and release to the seller only after a licensed vet exam confirms the animal is healthy and the microchip matches.
customer: First-time online puppy and kitten buyers (mostly Gen Z and millennials), plus ethical breeders, rescues and rehoming sellers who lose sales to scammers. Partner clinics are the fulfillment side and insurers are the third payer.
problem: Pet-purchase scams are a top online-fraud category inside the FTC's record $15.9B of 2025 scam losses. Deposits go by Zelle, Cash App or gift card and are irreversible. Legitimate breeders cannot prove trustworthiness. Sick puppies (parvo and congenital problems) show up days after a sale, and a vet shortage means new-patient slots are scarce, so buyers skip the check.
solution: The buyer pays via card or ACH into escrow. Release requires a 72-hour exam at a partner clinic confirming health, microchip and vaccination records; failure means refund minus fee. Part of the escrow fee pays the clinic for the exam, so the clinic gains a new client with prepaid revenue. The exam visit also enrolls the pet in insurance while it is clean of pre-existing conditions, for an acquisition fee. Extensions: lost-pet reward escrow released on a microchip scan, and stud and rehoming fees.
why_now: Record scam losses and irreversible peer-to-peer payments make buyers and platforms desperate for protection. Only 48.2% of practices proactively recommend insurance, so insurers need better first-year distribution. Clinics are capacity-constrained and want reliable new patients. Delayed-payout marketplace payment APIs make escrow cheap to build.
revenue_model: 4-5% escrow fee, $40-60 insurer acquisition fee per enrolled pet, and clinic exam fees funded from the escrow. Sellers can pay for a verified-breeder badge.
non_obvious_insight: The vet exam is the only trusted, licensed, in-person oracle in the pet-purchase chain, so use it as the escrow release condition. Because the fee funds the visit, the clinic gets a paid new client, which turns the vet shortage into a pull instead of a friction.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 ethical breeders or rescues and 5 clinics in one metro. Build on Stripe Connect delayed payouts. Market to breed groups on Facebook and puppy-advice communities, and offer the first 50 transactions at a discount for testimonials.

title: Meeting Subtext Captions for Neurodivergent Workers
one_liner: An on-screen coach for Zoom and Teams that flags conversational subtext (a question aimed at you, a topic shift, rising frustration) and supports post-meeting debriefs, sold through autism and ADHD coaches.
customer: Autism and ADHD coaching practices ($40-60 per client per month), employer neurodiversity hiring programs, and state vocational rehabilitation agencies.
problem: Autistic and ADHD adults often lose jobs and friendships over unspoken social subtext rather than skill. Human job coaches cost $75-150 an hour and cannot sit in every meeting. Loneliness among autistic adults is severe, and existing tools are scripts and courses that do not work in the live moment.
solution: A client-side app reading a live transcript and showing three private cue types ('direct question to you', 'time to wrap up', 'tone: irritated'), plus post-meeting debriefs shared with the coach and a rehearsal mode simulating hard meetings. Data stays local by default, and the coach dashboard shows patterns, not raw transcripts.
why_now: Real-time multimodal models now handle affect and conversational structure at low latency. Hybrid work makes meeting transcripts routine. Employers' neurodiversity hiring programs are maturing and need retention tools.
revenue_model: Per-seat license through coaching practices, employer accommodation budgets, and state vocational rehabilitation contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The right entry point is the coach's toolkit, not the consumer app. Coaches already have the trust, the payer relationship and the clinical framing, and AI extends their reach into moments they cannot attend.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 neurodiversity coaches through ADHD and autism coach networks. Pilot with 30 clients at $50 each, collect cue accuracy ratings and coach feedback, then approach two employers' neurodiversity leads.
